links.reason: The fragment's ground is பாரித்த தெல்லாம் வினையின் பயன், the Siddhar's is நன்மையும் தீமையும் பங்கயத்தோன் எழுதாப்படி வருமோ; both counsel the same unmoved calm (பொலிவின்றி நின்றான், சலியாதிரு). The incompatibility holds only if Brahma's writing is read as independent of one's deeds, which the note does not state, and the Siddhar's point is steadiness, with the agent incidental, so the tension is thinner than claimed.
links.text_issue: The marker flags the verse's sense as uncertain; who plotted the killing (கொலை சூழ்ந்த) is not stated.

links.reason: Naladiyar 48 asks கண்டிலர்கொல், as if seeing the vultures tear the corpse would end praise of sandal and garland; Valayapathi 70 says காலக் கனலெரியின் வேவன கண்டாலும் சால மயங்குவது, the heart is bewildered even having seen. The fragment sets a real limit on the quatrain's trust in sight, and both gains clauses name that limit specifically.

The shared word is only fresh water: in the Naladiyar புதுப்புனல் is the courtesan's love that ends when the rain (income) ends, while in the Valayapathi வெள்ளம் புதியது is the new man the fish (women) desert the old pond for, so the image does different work and is not one figure reworked. Teaches says the charge moves 'to the marriage', but காமனொடு ஆயினும் names Kama, not a husband or a marriage, and the epic-side gain that the fragment reworks the quatrain's figure is not shown.

Valayapathi 27 makes seizing and cutting the thief the theft's own பயன்; the Pandya says கள்வனைக் கோறல் கடுங்கோ லன்று, then, after the gem leaps from the anklet, பொன்செய் கொல்லன் தன்சொற் கேட்ட யானோ அரசன் யானே கள்வன். The epic supplies the case the rule does not foresee, the punisher who has not established the thief and becomes the criminal, and teaches names that limit.

Both rank a small food-gift: துற்றவிழ் ஒவ்வா (no gift equals a mouthful of rice) and உண்ணும் போது ஒரு கைப்பிடி, possible for all (யாவர்க்குமாம்). The pairing of 'easy' and 'supreme' is a real point, but the fragment's gesture (விரல்வைத்தது) belongs to a lost scene, and the epic-side gain that it is 'matched to a known practice of setting food aside before eating' reconstructs what the verse does not say; the relation is closer to develops than to a limit.
links.text_issue: Verse sense flagged uncertain; line 2 has a repaired ஃ.

links.reason: The fragment reworks Kuruntokai 17 phrase by phrase: மா என்று ... மடல் ஏறுப / மாவென மடலும் ஊர்ப, எருக்கின் இணர் / எருக்கங் கண்ணி, பிறர் ஆர்ப்ப / மறுகின் ஆர்க்கவும் படுப, காழ்க் கொள் / காமம் காழ் கொளினே. It adds புன்மை, பேய் and காம நோய், turning the lover's own general rule (தலைவன் கூற்று) into an outsider's diagnosis, which is exactly what teaches and both gains claim.
links.text_issue: Line 2 is damaged: யஎன்(று) is not a word (perhaps பூ என்று, as in Kuruntokai) and சுடுப may stand for சூடுப.

links.reason: 58 says courtesans leave the man of perished wealth (வீபொருளனை அகன்று) for a richer one like a beast moving to another's pasture; 65 says even the noble are left when wealth is spent (வெறுக்கை உலந்தால் ... போப), like birds from a fallen tree. The link is the same logic in two domains, courtesan and kin or followers, not one verse extending or fulfilling the other; teaches is true, but the type fits parallel_domain better.

Kural 377 has an apportioner (வகுத்தான் வகுத்த வகை) and the fragment makes தவம் the seed without which toil yields nothing (வித்தின்றிப் பைங்கூழ் ... தவம் இல்லான் ... இடர்ப்படும்). The contrast of agent and seed is real, but the verse does not say the austerity is past, and வகுத்தான் is ambiguous between fate and a personal agent, so the 'rival account of who apportions' needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Line 3 பொருளடு may be பொருளொடு with the vowel sign lost; line 3 opens with a stray யுய்த்தவம்.

links.reason: 16 asks பாயல் உய்யுமோ, whether the queen's bed escapes, while the king lingers in camp (பாசறை நீடினை); 19, by the same poet in the same decade, says he so loves the work of war (அவ்வினை மேவலை) that he grants no grace (யார்கொல் அளியை) to the modest wife who lives with him only in dreams (கனவினுள் உறையும்). The later poem turns the question into a charge and sets it beside the ravaged fields, which is a real development and not sequence.
links.text_issue: Lines 9-15 of 19 and 14, 18-19 of 16 are hard to construe; the readings of the queen's lines are tentative.

links.reason: Kural 957 sets the fault of the well-born high like மதிக்கண் மறு; Kundalakesi 17 says குற்றம் குற்றமே நல்ல ஆகா even in those who reached வாய்மை, and asks who would deny that the stain (கறை) on the throat of the forehead-eyed god is a stain. Both put a stain on an exalted body, and the fragment adds that height does not change a fault's nature and carries it from lineage to the gods; the gains are specific.

Naladiyar 283 states the loss only: no flower, no bees, so இலாஅர்க்கு இல்லை தமர். Valayapathi 65 adds the converse, தொழுமகன் ஆயினும் துற்றுடையானை ... சூழ்ப, the servant with food is surrounded, while the noble (விழுமியர்) is left, so the pair shows wealth outranking birth in both directions, which the quatrain does not state.

Both value children in the household (மக்கள் பயந்து மனையறம் / நன்கலம் நன்மக்கட் பேறு), but the argument against the courtesan rests on reading தோற்றம் ஒன்று இன்று as 'no issue', which the line may not mean. Kural 60 ties children to மனைமாட்சி, the wife's excellence, and gains nothing specific: 'a counter-case of what a life without the ornament lacks' is the shared theme restated.
links.text_issue: Line 1 has a typo, மக்க்ள் for மக்கள்.

links.reason: The shared figure is real, அந்தகன் அந்தகற்கு ஆறு சொலல் and குருடர்க்குக் கோல்காட்டிச் செல்லும் குருடர், but Tirumanthiram 2048 names no guru's grace or sight: its blind leader is as ignorant as the fragment's, so the guru-centred versus knowledge-centred contrast is read into it. The fragment does not limit the Saiva verse; same_image fits.

Kural 297 says if one keeps பொய்யாமை, not doing other virtues is good; Valayapathi 28 pairs பொய்யின்மை பூண்டு with அறநெறி ஆற்றுமின் and promises கௌவை இல் உலகு. The difference is real, but 297's sense depends on the division of its doubled words, and 'pays for it with a promise' is rhetoric; the qualification is thin.

Kural 330 reasons backward with என்ப: those in wretched bodies are said to be those who took life (உயிர் உடம்பின் நீக்கியார்), naming no former birth; Valayapathi 30, also on authority (கூறினர் அறிந்தார்), gives the frame, the four states (கதி நான்கினிடை நின்று தடுமாறும்) as killing's issue. The fragment supplies the rebirth scheme the couplet's inference needs, and each side gains something specific.

Kural 379 asks why those who take good as good (நல்லவாக் காண்பவர்) grieve when it fails, rebuking grief only; Kundalakesi 18 says அழுங்கார் உவவார், those who know neither grieve nor exult, since உறுவது உறும். The fragment's equanimity strikes out elation as well, a real tightening of the couplet's premise, as teaches says.

Both set grace above goods: அருளைப் பொருளா அறம்செய்தல் வேண்டும் and அருட்செல்வம் செல்வத்துள் செல்வம். That is largely agreement, and the fragment's afterlife clause (இருளியல் எய்தாதது) rests on an uncertain reading. The Kural-side gain, that its ranking is carried into a promise about the next world, is not new to the Kural, whose same chapter already denies the dark world to those with அருள்.
links.text_issue: Line 4 is read as இருள் இயல்பு எய்தாதது; sense flagged uncertain.

links.reason: The fragment's யான் எனது என்னலும் ஆமே answers Kural 346's யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு with an argument, a body of deeds (வினைய உடம்பு) that worms already feed and live in (நுகரவும் வாழவும்). Teaches and gains are true, but the fragment supplies the argument for the couplet's rule rather than limiting it, so develops fits, not qualifies.

Naladiyar 121 makes the belly of the senseless a burning ground (காடு) for beasts and birds; Valayapathi 18 says flesh-eaters have eaten their own kin (தம்சுற்றம் தின்றனர்) within the ocean of births. Joined, the burning ground holds one's relatives: the fragment supplies the kinship, the quatrain the funeral, and both gains name that.
links.text_issue: Line 2 is hard; its குற்றம் may stand for சுற்றம்.

links.reason: Acharakkovai 10 commands ஐயுறாது ஆடுக நீர் on ten occasions; Sivavakkiyar mocks those who bathe daily to remove dirt (அழுக்கறத் தினங்குளித்து) and asks where the dirt is. The conflict is defensible if the Acharakkovai's bath is read as removing the impurity the Siddhar means, but its uncleanness is ritual (வாலாமை, contact) while his is inner, and the note does not say which reading the tension depends on; teaches also brings in the Kural, which is not part of the link.
links.text_issue: Item list depends on counting ஊண்பொழுது and வைகு துயில் separately; ஏனை மயலுறல் is obscure.

links.reason: Naladiyar 183 says மறுமைக்கு வித்து மயலின்றிச் செய்து; Valayapathi 37 says for the state to come (செல்கதிக்கு), always and always (என்றும் என்றும்), like farmers who plough, make seed and water (விளைநிலம் உழுவார்போல் வித்துநீர் செய்துகொண்மின்). Both rest on transience (இளமையும் நிலையா / நிறம் வேறாம்), and the fragment turns the single seed into a continuing labour, a real extension.

5 says the learned found no guard for women (பெண்டிரைக் காப்பது இலம்); 26 says of women விரகிலர் and விடுத்தனர் முன்னே. The step from 'cannot be kept' to 'so let them go' holds only if விரகிலர் means no art avails and the ancients are the subject of விடுத்தனர், both uncertain; the verses are fragments in an editor's order, so the development is a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Sense of விரகிலர் and subject of விடுத்தனர் uncertain.

links.reason: Both have rain at the chaste wife's word (பெய்கெனப் பெய்தலும் / பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும் மழை), and the fragment lists it with the praise of country and town on the say of கூடல் ஆற்றவர். But teaches overreaches: the verse still says the rain falls when bidden, and listing it among honours does not make the rain 'the community's recognition of the wife rather than her private power'.

Kural 280 sets aside only shaving and long hair (மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும்) and tests the renouncer by what the world blames (உலகம் பழித்தது); Kundalakesi 4 dismisses a whole list, stripping or wrapping the body, dust, cold, fire, alms and matted hair (சடைத்தலையர்), as வார்த்தை, and puts tapas in a restrained life (மடிந்தொழுகல்). The two differ on where the proof of renunciation lies, as teaches says, and both gains hold.
links.text_issue: Speaker unnamed (என்றான்); reading of line 4 tentative, மடிந்து could mean 'as one dead'.

links.reason: Kural 1133's lover says in his own voice நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை பண்டுடையேன், now the madal; Valayapathi 23 condemns from outside the man struck by Kama's arrow who ignores the wise and elders and stains his fame (புகழ் மாசு படுப்பர்). The voice contrast is real but thin, and 23 does not itself name the madal, which comes in 24; the same point is made more strongly by the Kuruntokai link.

Both make women's faultless time short: அளிப்பவன் காணும் சிறுவரை and இழுக்கெனைத்தும் செய்குறாப் பாணி சிறிதே, even under a guard of swords (வாள்வாய்க் கிடந்தும்). The claimed difference, that the provider's gaze buys some steadiness where armed guard does not, rests on two disputed lines (துணைவனைக் கையார், and the quatrain's condition இழுக்கினைத் தாம்பெறுவராயின்), so it needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Verse sense flagged uncertain; துணைவனைக் கையார் is hard.

links.reason: Kural 1047 limits its rule to அறஞ்சாரா நல்குரவு and names only the mother (ஈன்றதாயானும்); Valayapathi 63 drops the moral condition and extends desertion to women, kin and children (பெண்டிர் மதியார் ... தம் மக்களும் ஒட்டார்) on lack of wealth alone (வெறுக்கை இலராயின்). Setting the two side by side shows the Kural's qualifier doing work, and both gains hold.
links.text_issue: Line 2 and வெண்டறை are uncertain; line 2 has a repaired ஃ.

links.reason: Kural 259 weighs one abstention from killing above a thousand oblations (அவிசொரிந்து ஆயிரம் வேட்டலின்); Valayapathi 13 says கொள்ளன்மின் கொலை கூடி வரும் அறம், refuse any dharma that comes with killing. The step from ranking merits to disqualifying a killing rite as dharma is real and stated in teaches; both gains are specific.

Kural 1062 curses the maker of the world if one must live even by begging (இரந்தும் உயிர்வாழ்தல்); Purananuru 393 is a bard's plea in hunger (அடல்நசை மறந்த எம் குழிசி) that laments there is no one in other lands who knows the duty of feeding (கடனறியாளர் பிறநாட்டு இன்மையின்). The poem does not present asking as an honourable calling; that rests on one reading of குடிமுறை பாடி, and the Kural's own chapter on asking allows asking from the generous, so the tension is a shared topic dressed up.
links.text_issue: Line 22 has a gap; line 2 has edition variants.

links.reason: 33 says those who never went near wealth renounce best (துன்னாது ஒழிந்தார் துறவோ விழுமிதே); 44 asks what shame there is in crossing the wasteland for wealth that feeds hungry kin (புலம்பில் பொருள்தரப் புன்கண்மை உண்டோ). The opposition is real, but 44's speaker is unknown and may be a view the work answers, and teaches says the editor set the two 'side by side' when they are eleven verses apart.

7 says one need not mourn things whose nature is to perish (அழிதல் மாலைப் பொருள்களுக்கு அழிதல் வேண்டா); 9 asks நமக்கு நாம் அழாதது என்னோ, why we do not weep for ourselves who die daily. Teaches itself says the weeping in 9 is not the grief 7 forbids, so there is no incompatible claim; 9 limits 7 by separating mourning others from waking to one's own dying, which is qualifies.
links.text_issue: Sense of கண் அணி களையல் உற்றார் (7, line 4) uncertain.

links.reason: Purananuru 192's வாழ்தல் இனிதென மகிழ்ந்தன்றும் இலமே, முனிவின் இன்னாதென்றலும் இலமே matches Kundalakesi 18's அழுங்கார் உவவார் closely, each resting on an order of things (முறைவழிப் படூஉம் / உறுவது உறும்). That is agreement across books, not extension. The other-side gain is false: the Sangam poem is already a teaching on joy and bitterness and needs no 'later religious setting' to become one.

Pattinathar lines up fire, worm, earth, kite, jackal and dog each saying எனக்கு of the corpse he reared with love (பிரியமுடன் வளர்த்தேன்); Kundalakesi 14 finds the worms (புழுக்குலம் ... நுகரவும் வாழவும்) already feeding in the living body one calls எனது. Together, the claim 'mine' fails before death and after it, which neither verse shows alone.
links.text_issue: Line 2 is obscure, but the link rests on lines 3-4.

links.reason: Both use ghee on fire: நெய்யால் எரி நுதுப்பேம் என்றற்றால் and அகையழல் அழுவந் தன்னை நெய்யினால் அவிக்கலாமோ. The lover's ghee is gossip that feeds love, the ascetic's is indulgence that feeds desire, a meaningful shared use; teaches and gains say so. The fragment neither limits nor conditions the couplet, so same_image is the right type.

Both call the human body rare (மனிதரின் அரியது ஆகும் தோன்றுதல் / அரும்பெறல் யாக்கை), the fragment from many karma-driven bodies (வினைபல வலியினாலே வேறுவேறு யாக்கை), the quatrain drawing the duty to press out its fruit. But teaches says the fragment's second rarity, wealth to enjoy (இனியவை நுகர எய்தும் செல்வம்), is what the quatrain says to turn into virtue; the quatrain speaks of the body like cane, not of wealth, so that clause is untrue.

Valayapathi 20 says practise அருந்தவம் and, going to the state without darkness, இனி இவண் வாரீர், with no god granting it; Tirumanthiram 272 says even burning one's bones and frying one's flesh (என்பே விறகா இறைச்சி அறுத்திட்டு) cannot reach the Lord except for those who melt in love (அன்போடு உருகி). On the reading teaches names, tapas sufficient by itself, the two make incompatible claims about what reaches release, the kind of tension this round tests.
links.text_issue: Line 1 பொருளடு may be பொருளொடு with the vowel sign lost; அருளுதல் சான்ற may mean 'full of compassion' rather than 'fit for grace', which would soften the conflict.

links.reason: Kural 741 says a fort serves both those who march out and those who fear (அஞ்சித் தற்போற்றுபவர்); 775 calls blinking before a spear flight for the fierce (வன்கணவர்க்கு). These are different situations, the state's defence and the single warrior's valour, and the brief excludes different advice for different situations from tension; teaches only restates the topic.
